correctness.rationale: For iid parents, the event has exactly one doubled atom, with exact probability 6(S2-2S3+2S4-S2^2). Under a two-mass split the objective is affine in ab with coefficient c=-2+6(a+b)-4(a+b)^2+4 R2. Compactness on each finite simplex and merge/equalize force a uniform maximizing law. The value 6(r-1)(r-2)/r^3 has its strict integer maximum 72/125 at r=5. Finite nonuniform equality cannot persist through flat merges, because splitting a uniform-five atom has c=-8/25. The power-sum limit covers countably many atoms and diffuse mass; de Finetti covers infinite exchangeability. Exact rational verification checked 126 compositions, 36 pair deformations and uniform support through 100; these are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural and nonroutine sharp four-sample occupancy event in Zhu’s explicitly motivated feasible-K_n law problem: exactly one repeated pair. Five equal masses, rather than the four draws or the three observed types, uniquely maximize among finite parents. The mass-split affine principle reduces arbitrary heterogeneous distributions to a one-parameter uniform support census and does not claim the still-unproved full-law convex-hull conjecture.
